row.evidence: NetSuite's Help Center documents SAML and OIDC SSO where admins create roles and assign users to them in NetSuite; it documents no SCIM endpoint, and Okta's NetSuite provisioning runs over NetSuite's SOAP web services.
row.notes: Status unchanged (none). netsuite.com (pricing.shtml, products.shtml, home) returned HTTP 403 to curl, the headless renderer (ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES) and WebFetch, so June's pricing URL could not be re-cited; pricing_page_url points to the Help Center page on licensing instead (licences are counted against the Full User Count purchased; no public price list). June's 'All pricing Contact Sales' is kept as Contact Sales without a fresh first-party quote. No SCIM: the Oracle NetSuite Help Center table of contents (24,795 entries) has no SCIM topic. Provisioning is through NetSuite's own SOAP/REST web services (employee record: add, update, delete, give access, roles): Okta's own NetSuite app provisions over SOAP web services with token-based auth (api_connector, Okta-built), and an Aquera-built OIN connector also exists (third party). SAML and OIDC SSO are features enabled per account; plan or edition gating is not stated.

scim.notes: False by absence (no SCIM topic anywhere in the Help Center); IdP provisioning uses NetSuite web services instead. Manual deprovisioning: inactivating the employee record removes access but keeps employment history, and inactive users stop counting against the Full User Count (c1, c4, c5).

capabilities.notes: Users are employee records; SOAP also offers get/search/upsert on employee. Giving access and assigning roles are fields/sublists on the employee record in the UI; API coverage of those was not confirmed.

endpoints.purpose: SOAP web services operations on the employee record

rate_limits.text: Concurrency limits based on service tier plus 10 per SuiteCloud Plus licence (e.g. shared service with one licence = 15).

limitations.text: Okta notes that with token-based authentication it cannot create or update users with Administrator or Full Access roles (NetSuite security restriction).

user_api.notes: Also a SOAP API (SuiteTalk SOAP Web Services) with the same employee record; RESTlets (custom scripts) are a third option.

okta.notes: OIN page ticks SAML, SWA, SCIM and Create/Update/Deactivate/Group Push (read from page markup), but Okta's provisioning guide requires NetSuite SOAP web services and token-based auth; NetSuite has no SCIM endpoint. A separate 'Netsuite Provisioning Connector by Aquera' is third-party built (c17).

entra.notes: Gallery SSO tutorial only (no provisioning tutorial; saas-apps/netsuite-provisioning-tutorial 404). Microsoft claims JIT provisioning; see conflicts.

conflicts.text: Microsoft's Entra tutorial says NetSuite supports just-in-time user provisioning enabled by default, while NetSuite's own SAML guide requires admins to assign users to SAML roles in NetSuite before sign-in and never mentions JIT.
